name_en: Local compactness theorem (exact theorem identity open)
canonical_name: Properties of locally compact spaces (topic family; exact proposition open)
statement_blocker: The catalog gloss names an open-ended theorem family, not a proposition. It fixes neither a local-compactness convention nor separation assumptions, binders, hypotheses, conclusion, or boundary cases, and it does not choose among characterization, neighborhood-basis, preservation, regularity, Baire, compact-open, or compactification results. Selecting one would invent or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix the ambient type and topology, universe levels, local-compactness convention, separation axioms, subspace/product/quotient structures if any, and every required typeclass assumption.
conclusion: Open: the catalog does not select a definition, characterization, preservation theorem, regularity or Baire consequence, compact-open result, or compactification theorem.
degenerate_case_status: No case is silently excluded before an exact source proposition is selected; empty, singleton, compact, discrete, non-Hausdorff, product, subspace, quotient, empty-neighborhood, and empty-compact-set cases remain pending source review.

compact refinement inside every neighborhood of every point

regularity, Baire, or compact-open topology consequences
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty and singleton spaces, compact spaces, and discrete spaces
non-T0, non-T1, non-R1, nonregular, and non-Hausdorff spaces

open, closed, and locally closed subspaces
empty, finite, and infinite products or function spaces

a product, subspace, quotient, embedding, Baire, regularity, or compact-open theorem used as the generic root
a structure, predicate, axiom, certificate, or hypothesis that assumes the desired result
